provenance.scope: finite v0 public seed corpus; hidden holdout remains a separate future deliverable

cases.rationale: A semantically verified Evidence record reports the exact JCS-normalized value under matching subject, operation and represented environment scope.
RFC 8785 canonicalization gives JSON number tokens 42 and 42.0 the same ECMAScript binary64 serialization.
The same scope and predicate report a different normalized numeric value.
One same-scope premise supports while another contradicts; no majority vote or provider-count uplift is permitted.
The evidence subject digest differs from the requested subject.
The operation differs from the requested operation.
REA Evidence v1 does not encode platform_version, so a version-specific claim cannot be supported.
The claim references a valid Evidence ID that was not supplied for replay.
A v0 Evidence observation is not an authenticity proof; no positive rule exists for this predicate.
The evaluator has no verifier for the stated assumption, so it cannot produce positive support.
Changing a supported result's disposition to refuted must be rejected even when the old derivation digest remains well-formed.
The exact request digest binds the falsification condition; an old result cannot be replayed against a changed request.
Raw claim parsing rejects duplicate JSON keys recursively before schema interpretation.
A nullable result field must be explicitly present; omitted is not equivalent to null.
Result schemas are closed and reject unrecognized fields.
The same semantic Evidence ID cannot be supplied twice to the replay set.
Replay cannot silently expand the exact premise set beyond the claim's ordered Evidence references.
Representation-only numeric token differences in the serialized result are equivalent under RFC 8785 canonicalization.
result.requested_evidence_ids contains a malformed Evidence ID
result evidence assessments must refer only to request premises
result assessment identifiers must be unique
result missing IDs must be members of the exact request premise set
a result Evidence ID cannot be both assessed and missing
